# Jung — Psychology and Religion: West and East, CW 11 (1969)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected carrier is volume 11 of Jung's *Collected Works*, *Psychology and Religion: West and East*, edited by Herbert Read, Michael Fordham, and Gerhard Adler and translated by R. F. C. Hull. JSTOR and library catalogues confirm the 1969 Princeton edition, its 699 pages, and its collection of Jung's major shorter writings on religious phenomena.

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** C. G. Jung, *Psychology and Religion: West and East*, trans. R. F. C. Hull, *The Collected Works of C. G. Jung*, vol. 11 (Princeton University Press, 1969), {paragraph or page}.

**Shortened note:** Jung, *Psychology and Religion*, {paragraph or page}.

**Bibliography:** Jung, C. G. *Psychology and Religion: West and East*. Translated by R. F. C. Hull. *The Collected Works of C. G. Jung*, vol. 11. Princeton University Press, 1969.

## Essay use

This is the primary Jung carrier for the braid's specific claim that religious images can be treated as psychic realities without being reduced either to external metaphysical objects or to disposable error. It gives the §4 return a proper source distinct from *Aion*, whose work in the corpus remains Self, symbolic totality, and quaternity.

**Claim boundary:** the selected local digital witness has now been read for the numbered passages below. They support attributed paraphrase of Jung’s psychological interpretation. His comparative histories, theological reconstructions and generalisations retain his attribution and their own evidential limits. No exact quotation or physical-event claim is certified here. QL’s authorial `X/x` retains its native derivation.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q001` — Sophia across named textual witnesses
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q001

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung brings Proverbs’ pre-existent feminine Wisdom through the Chochma/Logos comparison and an explicit Śakti comparison, then Ecclesiasticus and Wisdom of Solomon. Speech, cosmic pervasion, mediation and reflective wisdom develop a source-specific sequence. His proposed historical contacts are his claims; the comparison does not assign Taylor’s fixed three-office Sophia/Logos/Śakti formula to Jung.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§609–613; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q002` — The witness makes divine self-reflection consequential
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q002

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung juxtaposes the oppression of the righteous with Job’s trial, then reads Yahweh’s treatment of the faithful witness as a crisis requiring remembrance of Sophia and self-knowledge. This is Jung’s interpretation of the God-image, distinct from the biblical book’s narrated ending.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§614–617; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q003"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q003` — Familial and creation reconstruction between the two readings
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q003

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung reconstructs Adam/Eve, Cain/Abel, Satan and Lilith through his account of creation, divine faithfulness and Sophia’s return. This intervening sequence keeps his movement toward incarnation visible. Its historical and gender generalisations remain attributed to Jung; they do not define the native QL poles.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§618–624; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q004"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q004` — Bodily priority and the perfection/completeness difficulty
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q004

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung gives the Second Eve temporal and material priority: the God-man is born through a woman. Mary is interpreted through Sophia’s mediating office. He then argues that extraordinary purification can remove mother and son from ordinary humanity and impair the feminine completeness meant to compensate perfection. The source therefore preserves a difficulty within exaltation itself before renewing the mother–son/Logos relation.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§625–628; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q005"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q005` — Continuing incarnation and personal representation
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q005

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung turns toward responsibility in the empirical creature, interprets the 1950 Assumption declaration through longing for an intercessor and continuing incarnation, and insists that psychic reality is consequential. He asks for personal feminine representation while expressly distinguishing his psychological account from the dogmatic assertion that Mary is a goddess. His account of Catholic/Protestant difference remains his own interpretation.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§746–754; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

<a id="jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q006"></a>
## Passage card — `jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q006` — Conscious individuation and the scope of the God-image
^jung-1969-psychology-religion-cw11-q006

**Source-matched paraphrase:** Jung relates the nuptial image to further incarnation and conscious individuation. Conscious encounter changes the process through symbols and the relation of opposites. His closing qualification places the God-image with the archetype of the Self rather than identifying it with the unconscious as a whole. This empirical/psychological boundary remains distinct from Taylor’s native metaphysical derivation.

- **Locator:** *Answer to Job*, §§755–757; selected Hull digital witness identified above.
- **Status:** source-matched paraphrase; exact quotation unprepared.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased / argued from, as declared at the consumer.
- **Verification:** selected numbered primary paragraphs and surrounding context read on 2026-09-08; no full-volume or visual-page collation claimed.

### Whole consumers and distinct returns

[Mother, Assumption and chiasm](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/frank-taylor/mother-assumption-chiasm/WHOLE.md#mother-body-received) **consumes** the Sophia, Mary, completeness and conscious-individuation sequences. [Job’s separate Jung reception](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/biblical/job/WHOLE.md#job-jung-second-whole) **consumes** the selected witness/self-reflection movement. Their Taylor-authored operations retain their own provenance. These selected passages improve the source footing of those comparisons without certifying every assertion in Jung’s broader reading of Job or the independent historical doctrines to which he refers.
